quiz.question: What constitutes the strongest, most defensible technical evidence that network segmentation is functioning correctly?
options: A network diagram illustrating separated switches and colored subnets
VLAN IDs being configured with different numerical values in switch NVRAM
Empirical test results demonstrating that permitted business flows succeed while prohibited cross-segment flows are actively dropped by policy
Deploying an enterprise router with high CPU capacity
quiz.explanation: Diagrams and configuration files show intent, not enforcement. Definitive evidence requires empirical positive testing (permitted flows succeed) and negative testing (unauthorized cross-segment attempts are actively blocked and logged by the firewall).

quiz.question: What essential safeguard must an engineer execute prior to initiating a controlled failure or link-severance test in a lab?
options: Delete the original device configurations to force dynamic convergence
Save a known-good configuration baseline, document expected failover behavior, and verify telemetry collection
Disable all Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) instances simultaneously
Double the interface MTU to 9000 bytes across all access trunks
quiz.explanation: Before injecting faults, engineers must capture a known-good baseline configuration and state, define the expected recovery outcome, and ensure observability tools are actively logging so the event can be analyzed and safely restored.

quiz.question: In an 802.1Q tagged Ethernet frame, what is the role and size of the Tag Protocol Identifier (TPID) field?
options: It is 2 bytes long with a fixed value of 0x8100, identifying the frame as an 802.1Q tagged frame
It is 4 bytes long and contains the destination IP address of the router sub-interface
It is 12 bits long and specifies the VLAN ID (1 to 4094)
It is 3 bits long and defines the Spanning Tree root bridge priority
quiz.explanation: The 802.1Q header is 4 bytes total: the first 2 bytes are the Tag Protocol Identifier (TPID), set to 0x8100. This signals to switches and network cards that an 802.1Q tag follows (containing 3-bit PCP, 1-bit DEI, and 12-bit VLAN ID).

quiz.question: Why should an enterprise Guest Wi-Fi subnet (e.g., VLAN 30) have a default-deny policy toward all internal subnets?
options: To prevent guest laptops from exhausting the DHCP lease pool on the core router
To isolate untrusted personal/guest devices and prevent lateral movement or scanning against internal databases and servers
Because guest devices cannot process TCP window scaling headers
To force guest devices to use IPv6 link-local addresses exclusively
quiz.explanation: Guest devices are untrusted by definition (unmanaged, lack EDR, unknown malware status). Isolating the guest segment prevents malicious actors or infected guest laptops from scanning, attacking, or moving laterally into internal server and management zones.

quiz.question: In a high-availability first-hop redundancy protocol (HSRP / VRRP), how does tuning timers from standard (3s hello / 10s hold) to millisecond intervals affect network convergence?
options: It increases convergence time from seconds to minutes
It reduces link failure detection and failover time from ~10 seconds down to sub-second (<800ms) recovery at the cost of slight control-plane CPU overhead
It converts stateful TCP sessions into stateless UDP datagrams
It eliminates the need for virtual IP addresses on the gateway
quiz.explanation: Standard HSRP timers (3s hello, 10s hold) cause a ~10-second blackout before a standby router claims the virtual IP. Millisecond timers (e.g. 250ms hello, 750ms hold) detect dead routers in under a second, minimizing packet drops and preventing TCP session timeouts.

quiz.question: What does a packet capture (PCAP) collected via Wireshark or tcpdump prove during network troubleshooting?
options: It proves that the entire enterprise network is free of vulnerabilities
It proves the exact packets and protocol interactions that traversed that specific capture interface at that specific point in time
It proves that the server CPU has zero hardware defects
It proves that the routing protocol will never flap in the future
quiz.explanation: A packet capture is an authoritative record of what crossed a specific physical or virtual interface during the capture window. It proves whether packets reached that point, whether TCP handshakes completed, and whether errors or resets occurred, but only at that observation point.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Router-on-a-Stick (ROAS) and Layer 3 Switch Virtual Interfaces (SVIs) for inter-VLAN routing?
options: ROAS requires physical cables for each VLAN, while SVIs require wireless connections
ROAS routes traffic across an external physical trunk link to a router sub-interface, whereas SVIs route traffic internally within switch ASIC hardware at wire speed
ROAS cannot enforce access control lists (ACLs)
SVIs are only supported on unmanaged home consumer switches
quiz.explanation: Router-on-a-Stick routes inter-VLAN traffic out of the switch across a single trunk link to a router with 802.1Q sub-interfaces ('hairpinning'). Layer 3 switches with Switch Virtual Interfaces (SVIs) route between VLANs directly inside the switch backplane using hardware ASICs at line rate.

quiz.question: In an enterprise network engineering report, why is documenting 'Residual Risks & Limitations' a mandatory section?
options: It allows engineers to avoid taking responsibility for project failures
No network design eliminates all risk; identifying known single points of failure, budget tradeoffs, and operational caveats enables informed leadership governance
It is required by the BGP RFC 4271 specification for route reflectors
It automatically reduces the likelihood score on the risk register to zero
quiz.explanation: Engineering integrity requires transparency. Documenting residual risks (e.g., lack of redundant power supplies, single ISP uplink, or unencrypted legacy IoT protocols) provides organizations with a clear roadmap for future improvements and risk mitigation.

quiz.question: When running an `iperf3` throughput test, why should an engineer record test duration, parallel stream count, and host resource utilization alongside the bandwidth number?
options: Single-stream tests on high-latency links are limited by TCP window size; documenting parameters ensures tests are scientifically reproducible and explainable
Because iperf3 crashes if parallel streams are not documented in the terminal
To calculate the BGP autonomous system path prepending count
To prevent switches from discarding 802.1Q trunk tags
quiz.explanation: Network throughput is heavily influenced by TCP window scale, latency, stream count, and CPU bottlenecks. Recording the exact methodology ensures results can be validated and reproduced by other engineers under identical conditions.

quiz.question: Which sequence correctly reflects the 5-phase engineering lifecycle for building an enterprise network capstone?
options: Construct -> Test -> Assess -> Design -> Scope
Scope & Design -> Construct Topology -> Implement Services & Controls -> Verify & Troubleshoot -> Assess & Present
Test -> Deploy -> Design -> Reverse -> Report
Purchase Hardware -> Connect Cables -> Disable Firewalls -> Ping -> Finish
quiz.explanation: A structured engineering lifecycle moves methodically from Phase 1 (Scope & Design), Phase 2 (Construct Topology), Phase 3 (Implement Services & Controls), Phase 4 (Verify & Troubleshoot), to Phase 5 (Assess, Document, & Present).
